questions.prompt: Why did packet switching suit computer traffic better than the phone network's circuit switching?

options: The first personal computers
The first email programs
Packet-forwarding machines between each host and the network: the first routers

Every ARPANET host switched to TCP/IP, which became the standard protocol between networks
ARPANET sent its first message, from UCLA to SRI

options: The Internet grew by the same number of hosts every year
The Internet stopped growing

options: 128-bit addresses instead of 32-bit
Multicast replaces broadcast
Hosts can configure their own addresses from the network prefix

options: Physical, Network, Data Link, Transport, Session, Application, Presentation
Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
Data Link, Physical, Network, Transport, Presentation, Session, Application
Physical, Data Link, Transport, Network, Session, Presentation, Application

questions.prompt: Which OSI layer handles encoding, compression, and encryption?
options: Session
Transport
Presentation
Data Link

questions.prompt: The TCP/IP model's Network Access layer covers which OSI layers?
options: Network and Transport
Data Link and Network
Session, Presentation, and Application

questions.prompt: During encapsulation, what is the unit of data called at the network layer, and at the data link layer?
options: Packet, then frame

Frame, then packet

Network: the destination IP address

options: The data link header's MAC addresses
The transport header's port numbers
The application data

options: Tunnels make the network slower
Tunnels can only be used by administrators
A firewall that checks only the outer headers can't see the traffic hidden inside an allowed protocol
Tunneled packets skip the physical layer
